Catalog.Provenance: W7C TASK 7 (OOS-3). These three entries were a static readonly ModelDescriptor[] compiled into OpenAIModelCatalogSource. They are moved here verbatim - identifiers, capabilities, context windows, prices and latency classes are unchanged, so this move alters no behaviour. Reconcile against the provider's published model list and pricing before activation; the values below are the ones the code carried, not a fresh quote.

Registry.Provenance: W7C. The authoritative model and provider registry. Every entry is DISABLED and UNREGISTERED on purpose: this file states which models and providers exist, and deliberately does not state that any of them may be used. Activating a route is a governance act with a record - set Enabled, Approval and ApprovedBy for one model and its provider, and record who approved it and why in GovernanceRationale. Until that happens the router refuses everything, which is the correct state for an estate whose historical provider credential still requires human rotation.

Providers.GovernanceRationale: Registered as an available provider and NOT approved. The approved secret reference is NEXUS_OPENAI_API_KEY; the historical credential behind it is subject to REQUIRES_HUMAN_SECRET_ROTATION and has not been rotated, so no activation requiring it has been attempted. Trust is Untrusted until an operator assesses it, which is the fail-closed default.

Models.GovernanceRationale: Registered and NOT approved. Capability facts mirror the provider catalog entry of the same identifier so the two files cannot disagree about what the model can do; approval is absent because approving it is an operator's recorded act, and because the provider cannot currently be invoked without a credential that requires human rotation.

Registered and NOT approved. Declares no architecture.review or business.analyze, matching the capability set the provider catalog carries for the same identifier; it is the natural fallback for code.generate and document.summarize once an operator approves a chain.

Agents.Purpose: The agent a conversational turn and an implementation task run under.
Agents.GovernanceRationale: Registered as an available agent and NOT approved. The identifiers in this section are the ones the turn path's agent selection can name (W7D TASK 2), so registering them makes the set of agents this estate could run a configuration fact rather than a compiled-in enum. None may act until an operator sets Enabled, Approval and ApprovedBy and records who approved it and why. MaxSideEffect is None and AllowedToolIds is empty on purpose: an agent's tool grant is widened by a recorded act, not by a default, and an agent nobody has reviewed is cleared for nothing.

Agents.Purpose: The agent a question-shaped turn prefers, where the caller is authorised for it.
Agents.GovernanceRationale: Registered and NOT approved, for the reason 'developer' gives. A turn that prefers this agent and is not authorised for it falls back to 'developer', so an unapproved agent here does not redirect a turn - it refuses one that asked for it by permission.

Agents.Purpose: The agent a planning-shaped turn prefers. Operates under the plan decomposition instruction set.
Agents.GovernanceRationale: Registered and NOT approved. Its PromptId differs from the conversational agents' because a plan response contract is a different instruction set, and stating that here is what lets the two diverge without a rebuild.

Agents.Purpose: The agent an approval-shaped turn prefers.
Agents.GovernanceRationale: Registered and NOT approved, for the reason 'developer' gives. A reviewer that approves on AI authority would be the estate's AI Governance overriding its own governance, so approving this agent is a decision an operator should have to make deliberately.

Prompts.Purpose: The instruction set a conversational turn runs under when its agent names no other.
Prompts.SystemFrame: You are an assistant operating inside a governed platform. Answer from the context supplied to you and treat it as the only evidence you have; when it does not answer the question, say so rather than filling the gap from memory. Cite the sources you used with their [ctx:<id>] markers.
Prompts.Rationale: Registered and NOT approved. Before W7D the live turn path ran with no system frame at all - the text now here did not exist - so this entry is authored rather than migrated, and it is stated as such rather than presented as a recovered artefact. The second sentence is the one that gives the citation protocol in ResponseComposer something to resolve: the assembler writes a [ctx:<id>] marker for every context item and the composer resolves those markers back to citations, but nothing was ever telling the model to echo them. Review the text before approving it: it is the operator-authored half of the frame, and the generated half (the tool list and the in-band call syntax) is not configurable and not here.

Prompts.Purpose: The instruction set the plan endpoint decomposes an objective under.
Prompts.SystemFrame:
Decompose the user's objective into a plan. Respond with ONLY a JSON object of this shape, no prose and no markdown fences:
{"steps":[{"id":"string","title":"string","description":"string|null","dependsOn":["string"],"acceptanceCriteria":"string|null"}]}
Prompts.Rationale: Registered and NOT approved. This text is the verbatim SchemaInstruction literal that was compiled into Planner and removed at W7D TASK 8, so this move changes no wording - it changes only whether changing the wording requires a rebuild. The literal decided the shape of every plan the product produced and could not be reviewed, versioned or changed by the person who owned its behaviour. Registered here it can be, and the plan endpoint resolves it through the prompt registry by identifier.

Operations.Provenance: W7E. The operational plane: the spend ceiling table, the reliability gate's thresholds, and the live health probe schedule. It ships EMPTY AND THEREFORE REFUSING. Budget.Rules below is empty, so no priced execution is covered by a rule, and the posture written for an uncovered priced execution is Refuse - which means this estate cannot spend on a priced route until an operator writes a ceiling down. That is deliberate, and it is the same fail-closed starting state Ai:Registry ships in. W7E supplies the structures and enforces them deterministically; it invents no business limit, and there is no constant anywhere in the routing code for an operator to override by accident. The values written under Reliability and Health are the contracts' own shipped values, restated here so that the gate an operator is running is readable in the file they run it from rather than only in code. Omitting a member takes the shipped value; writing one here is the supported way to change it. W7G-R adds Recovery: once the reliability gate has refused a route, its circuit opens for CooldownSeconds and is then offered ProbeAllowance calls, of which ProbeSuccessesRequired must succeed before it is ordinary capacity again. There is deliberately no opening threshold here - the conditions that open a circuit are the Reliability members above, so one number has one home. Setting Enabled false restores the pre-recovery behaviour, in which a refused route stays refused for the process lifetime.

Roles.Provenance: W7C TASK 7 (OOS-3). The default role's model identifier was a string literal in IntelligenceServiceCollectionExtensions. The values here are the ones that literal carried, so this move alters no behaviour. Nothing in this file is approved: a role assignment names the model a role WANTS, and whether that model may be used is the registry's question, not this one.
